PH 101.desc: This course covers the basic principles of epidemiology, with applications to investigations of noninfectious (“chronic”) and infectious diseases. Explores various study designs appropriate for disease surveillance and studies of etiology and prevention. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 101. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 101 and PH 101.
PH 101.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.
PH 101.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior

PH 102.desc: Fundamentals of biostatistics and basic methods for analysis of continuous and binary outcomes for one, two, or several groups. Includes: summarizing and displaying data; probability; statistical distributions; central limit theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing; comparing means of continuous variables between two groups; comparing proportions between two groups; simple and multiple linear regression. Hands-on data analysis using software and statistical applications in public health. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 102. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 102 and PH 102.
PH 102.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.
PH 102.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior

PH 110.desc: This course introduces health behavior concepts through applications to chronic disease prevention. The focus is on smoking, dietary behaviors, and physical activity and is organized around relationships to health, measurement, influencing factors, interventions, and translation to public health practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 110. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 110 and PH 110.
PH 110.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.
PH 110.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Sophomore, Senior

PH 120.desc: This course covers the rationale for and effectiveness of policies to influence nutrition, physical activity, and substance use behavior. Policies include legalization, taxation, labeling, produce manufacturing, warning labels, licensing, marketing, and counter-marketing practices and restrictions on use. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 120. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 120 and PH 120.
PH 120.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and upper-division standing.

PH 130.desc: This core public health course addresses the fundamentals of environmental and occupational health, including identification of hazards, basic toxicology, risk assessment, prevention/protection, and regulatory/control policies. Specific environmental and occupational hazards and relevant case studies will be presented. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 130. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 130 and PH 130.
PH 130.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 101 or FMPH 101, and upper-division standing.
PH 130.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior

PH 151.t: Planning, Conducting, and Reporting Responsible and Ethical Research
PH 151.desc: This course is designed to encourage inquiry of and discussion about regulations, ethical principles, and organizational practices that support the responsible and ethical conduct of research. These concepts will be conveyed using select readings, current events, student-led presentations, and invited guest speakers.
PH 151.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing.

PH 151R.t: Planning, Conducting, and Reporting Responsible and Ethical Research
PH 151R.desc: This course is designed to encourage inquiry of and discussion about regulations, ethical principles, and organizational practices that support the responsible and ethical conduct of research. These concepts will be conveyed using select readings, current events, student-led presentations, and invited guest speakers.
PH 151R.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing. This is a distance education course. Students may only receive credit for one of these courses: PH 151, PH 151R, or FMPH 151.

PH 155.t: Qualitative Research for Global Public Health
PH 155.desc: An overview of the role of qualitative research methods in public health. The course will focus on qualitative research as it relates to formative program design, community-based participatory approaches, and as a tool for amplifying voices and elucidating both complex social-ecological processes and internal individual experiences. Throughout the term, students will work in teams to design, conduct, analyze, and report a full qualitative study on a public health topic of their choosing. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 155.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.

PH 156.t: Skills for Health Promotion and Communication
PH 156.desc: This introductory course prepares individuals for public health careers by developing essential communication skills for professional effectiveness. Participants will learn various strategies and techniques for clear and impactful communication across different audiences. The curriculum focuses on creating clear, concise messages and constructing compelling narratives for successful public health initiatives.
PH 156.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing.

PH 157.desc: This course will explore the intersection of oppressions based on social identities such as race, ethnicity, socioeconomic class, gender, and citizenship status. This course will introduce the framework of intersectionality, with an emphasis on its use within the field of public health and explore and analyze how race and ethnicity are socially constructed and intersect with identities to influence health behavior and outcomes.
PH 157.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing.

PH 161.desc: Clinical nutrition is the study of nutrition and diet as related to the prevention and treatment of human disease. The practical and psychosocial aspects of diet modification and food/food product availability are key aspects of clinical nutrition practice, whether individual or community based, irrespective of whether the goal is primary prevention or disease treatment. Students will identify applications and translation of nutritional guidelines and recommendations into behavior in the course. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 161.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.
PH 161.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Sophomore, Senior

PH 162.desc: This course aims to empower students to critically evaluate digital consumer technologies related to health by exploring the social, cultural, and political contexts in which they are designed and used. Students will learn how to evaluate digital consumer tools that are and can be used by the public to promote health and will investigate both the benefits and the unintended consequences of digital health, and the ways in which it can reinforce marginalization.
PH 162.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing.

PH 171.desc: This course consists of a series of practical epidemiological infectious and non-infectious disease paper- and computer-based exercises. Students will have the opportunity to apply their epidemiological and biostatistical skills to real-world situations. The course is highly interactive and challenges students’ knowledge and critical thinking capacities. Students will give presentations, write a scientific abstract and press release, and develop a poster. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 171.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PH 101 or FMPH 101. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.

PH 172.desc: This course addresses fundamentals of vaccine-preventable diseases and immunizations, with an emphasis on resources to maintain public health expertise in a continually evolving field.
PH 172.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing.

PH 191.desc: Selected topics in the field of public health. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. May be taken for credit up to three times.
PH 191.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Additional prerequisites may be required at instructor’s discretion. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Department approval required.
PH 191.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Sophomore, Senior

PH 193.desc: This is the first of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will integrate the skills and knowledge gained throughout the BSPH program and learn critical elements of public health research and practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 193.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, and PH 120 or FMPH 120. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only.
PH 193.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior; Limited to major: Public Health, PblHlth w/Con Biostatistics, PblHlth w/Con Clmt&EnvrnSci, PblHlth w/Con CmntyHlth Sci, PblHlth w/Con Epidemiology, PblHlth w/Con HlthPol&Mgmt, PblHlth w/Con Medicine Sci

PH 193R.desc: This is the first of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will integrate the skills and knowledge gained throughout the BSPH program and learn critical elements of public health research and practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 193R.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, and PH 120 or FMPH 120. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only. This is a distance education course. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PH 193, PH 193R, or FMPH 193.

PH 194.desc: This is the second of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will interpret and contextualize findings from their projects completed in the first part of the series. Oral and written presentations will focus on disseminating public health information in diverse formats. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 194.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, PH 120 or FMPH 120, and PH 193 or FMPH 193. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only.

PH 194R.desc: This is the second of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will interpret and contextualize findings from their projects completed in the first part of the series. Oral and written presentations will focus on disseminating public health information in diverse formats. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 194R.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, PH 120 or FMPH 120, and PH 193 or FMPH 193. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only. This is a distance education course. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PH 194, PH 194R, or FMPH 194.

PH 195P.desc: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. May be taken for credit up to two times.
PH 195P.pre: a minimum of A– in the course in which the student plans to assist, a 3.0 cumulative UC GPA, and instructor and department approval.
PH 195P.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior

PH 196AH.desc: This is the first of an accelerated two-part honors series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students review, reinforce, and complement skills and knowledge gained throughout the BSPH program, and prepare a proposal integrating critical elements of public health research and practice. This course represents an experiential learning opportunity at a pre-approved community site. Students will develop, refine, and implement a public health proposal. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 196AH.pre: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, PH 120 or FMPH 120. Department approval required. Restricted to upper-division public health majors only.

PH 196BH.desc: This is the second of an accelerated two-part honors series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health majors. Students will analyze, interpret, and contextualize findings from their projects completed in the series. Oral and written communication will focus on disseminating public health information in diverse formats, and will include a presentation and an honors thesis. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
PH 196BH.pre: PH 196AH. Department approval required. Restricted to upper-division public health majors only.

PH 199.desc: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Family Medicine and Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 199. PH 199 and/or FMPH 199 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
PH 199.pre: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.
PH 199.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior

PH 200.desc: This course provides students with an overview of the foundations of public health. It is organized into three modules: 1) science of public health (history, philosophy, core functions, causes of morbidity and mortality, and prevention), 2) factors related to human health (environmental, biological, genetic, behavioral, psychological, cultural, social, political, global, and ecological), and 3) public health leadership (leadership, management, negotiation, mediation, and interprofessional connections).
PH 200.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Behavior), MPH(Health Policy), MPH(Public Mental Health), MPH(Tech&Precision Health), MPH(Epidemiology), Biostatistics, Pub Hlth(Epidemiol)JT Doc SDSU, PubHlth(Health Behav)JtDocSDSU, PublHlth(Global Hlth)JtDocSDSU, PhD PbHl w/Con HlthSvcs&ImpSci

PH 220A.t: Advanced Methods in Health Services A
PH 220A.desc: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to causal inference methodologies essential for empirical research in public health. Students will explore the distinctions between association and causation, the impacts of biases, and the role of randomized experiments and assignment mechanisms. Students will develop the skills to evaluate research designs and implement appropriate statistical techniques to identify and estimate causal relationships in both observational and experimental data.

PH 221.desc: This course is designed to increase students’ knowledge, confidence, and capabilities in crafting scientific research proposals to support their dissertation research and post-doctoral careers. This includes the study of successful, funded applications; readings and discussions designed to enhance awareness of funding opportunities; exercises that enable students to understand and critique applications; and a series of writing assignments that will culminate in a proposal ready for submission.

PH 222.desc: This course examines the use of innovative methods that have been designed or tailored for use in monitoring, evaluating, and facilitating implementation of evidence-based programs, policies, and practices.

PH 231.desc: This course will provide an introduction to the definition, design, and practice of mixed methods research. Mixed methods approaches are becoming increasingly common in many research areas, especially in public health because of the combined use of qualitative and quantitative data sets. This course will teach you to meaningfully integrate the two and takes an applied focus.

PH 233.desc: This course encompasses a range of topics related to aging including the demography of aging, hallmarks of biological aging, physiological reserve and resilience, physical and cognitive function, major chronic diseases of aging (diabetes, kidney disease, heart disease, cancer, osteoporosis, fracture, Alzheimer’s disease, and related dementias), multimorbidity, and epidemiology of healthy aging.

PH 233L.desc: The objectives of the epidemiology of aging lab supplement are to familiarize students with aging cohorts, prominent biases, and methodological approaches to addressing them; commonly used statistical methods; and common areas of epidemiological research in aging populations.

PH 235.desc: Students will review funded and nonfunded grant proposals for different types of NIH awards, with an emphasis on R01 research awards. Students will have an opportunity to have their own proposals reviewed by instructors and classmates. The instructor will prepare a research proposal with help from the students.

PH 240.desc: This course examines life course research for health sciences. Emphasis will be placed on methodologies employed to estimate cumulative effects from earlier life exposures and biologic pathways to describe risks on health and disease across the life course.

PH 251.desc: The course introduces the fundamental concepts, principles, and methods in genetic epidemiology. The course reviews terminology used in genetics, introduces principles of population and human genetics, and provides an overview of the use of molecular and genetic methods in utilized genetic epidemiologic and clinical research. This includes the study designs used to identify the genetic basis of Mendelian and complex traits and diseases.

PH 258.desc: This course combines didactic instruction, interactive sessions, and student presentations. Topics cover study design, ethics, data analysis and management techniques, and qualitative research will be presented.
PH 258.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Pub Hlth(Epidemiol)JT Doc SDSU, PubHlth(Health Behav)JtDocSDSU, PublHlth(Global Hlth)JtDocSDSU

PH 259.desc: Students will explore an epidemiologic research question by reviewing relevant published literature, and then design and conduct appropriate data analysis using a preexisting dataset.
PH 259.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Pub Hlth(Epidemiol)JT Doc SDSU

PH 260.desc: Students will learn the principles of scientific writing, review examples of scientific literature, and then complete a manuscript suitable for publication based on their research project.

PH 261.desc: Students will learn the principles of scientific presentations for the classroom and for scientific meetings (both oral and poster presentations). Students will then prepare and deliver presentations based on their research project.

PH 270.t: Cultural Perceptions about Health and Disease
PH 270.desc: This course takes an interdisciplinary look at the relationship between culture and health in diverse sociostructural contexts.
PH 270.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: PublHlth(Global Hlth)JtDocSDSU

PH 275.desc: The HSRIS colloquium series is a program of empirical research seminars focused on the most important issues facing patients, providers, health care systems, and policymakers today. It provides an opportunity for HSRIS doctoral students across all stages of completion to meet regularly, analyze and critique ongoing research, and participate in stimulating discussion with HSRIS faculty and guest lecturers.

PH 277.t: Health Policy, Technology, and Public Health
PH 277.desc: This course provides an overview of the US health policy landscape. It addresses the development of explicit health policies to promote certain health behaviors, policies aimed at public health safety, and policy issues related to emerging health and biomedical technologies. Renumbered from FPM 290. Students may not receive credit for PH 277 and FPM 290.
PH 277.pre: must be enrolled in the UC San Diego/SDSU Joint Doctoral Program in public health (PU75, PU76, and PU77), biostatistics major (FM77), or consent of instructor.

PH 278.t: Scale Development for Behavioral Health Measurement
PH 278.desc: Course will present theory and methods for developing scales to assess public health-related constructs (e.g., physical, mental, and social well-being).

PH 280.t: Practicum in Global Health and Health Behavior
PH 280.desc: Students will learn about grant writing, project management, preparation of manuscripts for publication and presentations for scientific meetings, and also work individually with a faculty mentor in preparing manuscripts using data from a specific health behavior intervention.
PH 280.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: PubHlth(Health Behav)JtDocSDSU, PublHlth(Global Hlth)JtDocSDSU

PH 288.desc: The aim of this course is to introduce graduate students to the strengths and appropriate use of qualitative research and analysis methods, with specific application to public health research and policy. The course will use a combination of didactic, group, interactive, and applied techniques to teach knowledge and skills relevant to qualitative research. Lecture will present on the theory and ethical use of qualitative methods.

PH 289R.t: Dissemination and Implementation Science in Health: An Introduction
PH 289R.desc: This course will emphasize the unique aspects of dissemination and implementation research, including the types of questions it seeks to answer, the outcomes examined and how they differ from other types of studies, the models and frameworks commonly used, and the qualitative and quantitative methods employed.
PH 289R.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Pub Hlth(Epidemiol)JT Doc SDSU, PubHlth(Health Behav)JtDocSDSU, PublHlth(Global Hlth)JtDocSDSU, PhD PbHl w/Con HlthSvcs&ImpSci

PH 291.desc: Topics of special interest in public health. Topics may vary from quarter to quarter.
PH 291.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Pub Hlth(Epidemiol)JT Doc SDSU, PubHlth(Health Behav)JtDocSDSU, PublHlth(Global Hlth)JtDocSDSU

PH 296.desc: The practicum is designed to provide doctoral students with a short-term, field-based experience in community-engaged research. This student-led activity is expected to be implemented in collaboration with a sponsoring organization and under the supervision of a qualified site mentor or UC San Diego faculty researcher who conducts community-based studies or experiments that generate data in the medical, public health, or pharmacologic sciences.

PH 297.desc: Individual graduate study or research not covered by present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the School of Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member and track director prior to registering.
PH 297.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Pub Hlth(Epidemiol)JT Doc SDSU, PubHlth(Health Behav)JtDocSDSU, PublHlth(Global Hlth)JtDocSDSU

PH 299.desc: Public health doctoral program dissertation research units.

PH 40.desc: This course provides an introduction to the infrastructure of public health; the analytical tools employed by public health practitioners; bio-psychosocial perspectives of public health problems; health promotion/disease prevention; quality assessment in public health; and legal and ethical concerns. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 40. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 40 and PH 40.

PH 400.desc: Students will understand principles of measurement of clinical data, recognize data types, and determine statistical methods for analysis of a given dataset. They will gain experience in preparing a clinical dataset for analysis. Students will learn basic data visualization, statistical testing and inference, and statistical modeling with R.
PH 400.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.
PH 400.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Behavior), MPH(Health Policy), MPH(Public Mental Health), MPH(Tech&Precision Health), MPH(Epidemiology)

PH 401.desc: This course provides a foundational understanding of principles and methods used to study the distribution and determinants of health and disease in populations. Topics include study design, data collection, measures of disease frequency, and risk assessment. Through lectures and small group discussions, students learn to critically evaluate epidemiological research, understand the ethical considerations in conducting epidemiological studies, and recognize common sources of bias and confounding.
PH 401.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.
PH 401.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Behavior), MPH(Health Policy), MPH(Public Mental Health), MPH(Tech&Precision Health), MPH(Epidemiology)

PH 402.desc: This course provides an opportunity to explore the theoretical issues and current methodologies related to understanding and influencing health behavior change in diverse populations. The course will focus on the social, behavioral, and biologic determinants of health on the individual, interpersonal, community, institutional, and policy levels. The examples of application of theories to determinants and intervention research and disparities in health behavior and outcomes are covered.
PH 402.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

PH 403.desc: This course will focus on fundamental concepts in research design and measurement to understand methodological considerations in quantitative and qualitative scientific studies in public health and be able to critically evaluate public health research. Emphasis will be on creating testable hypotheses, designing a hypothetical study to test the hypothesis, and assessing methods of measurement.
PH 403.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

PH 404.t: Introduction to Environmental and Occupational Health
PH 404.desc: This course examines the relationship between human activities, the environment, and health. It explores how environments affect well-being, focusing on hazards from workplaces and contamination. It also addresses personal and societal behaviors impacting environmental health and reviews strategies to mitigate negative human effects at individual and community levels.
PH 404.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

PH 405.desc: This course will introduce students to health policy making and the organization and financing of health services in the United States, enhance their understanding of the historical and political context of health policy, and enable them to develop strategies for analysis of health policy issues. The course aims to convey not just specific facts, but to help students develop the ability and confidence to assess current health policy issues in a thoughtful, comprehensive, and rigorous manner.
PH 405.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

PH 406.desc: This course will prepare students for scientific writing in a variety of contexts. These may include scientific abstracts and research summaries, plain language summaries, op-eds, community engagement, and using LLMs. The course will incorporate group projects as well as individual assignments.
PH 406.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

PH 410.desc: This course focuses on critical analyses of health behavior theories and their applications to interventions in multiple fields, such as (but not limited to) nutrition, cancer, and physical activity. The course will prepare students to design, plan, implement, and evaluate health behavior interventions covering individual and population approaches to behavior change.
PH 410.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB87) or program approval and successfully completed PH 402.

PH 411.desc: This course covers study designs to iteratively optimize and evaluate public health programs such as a proof-of-concept trial, randomized controlled trial, sequential multiple assignment randomized trial, factorial screening trial, microrandomized trial, stepped wedge trial, single case experiments, and nonrandomized study designs. The course includes a philosophical grounding on why evidence is important and what underlying assumptions undergird “evidence-based practice.”
PH 411.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB87, PB90, and PB75) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 402 or PH 402, and FMPH 403 or PH 403.

PH 412.desc: This course is focused on the principles of health promotion and health communication, examining the societal impact and needs, behavioral change theory, and study designs to develop and evaluate interventions. Effective communication techniques used to promote behavior change, disseminate evidence, and communicate risk in today’s multimedia world are highlighted, including cultural tailoring. Students serially develop and apply these strategies in the design of a public health campaign of their choice.
PH 412.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB90) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 402 or PH 402.

PH 413.t: Ethics in Public Health Research and Practice
PH 413.desc: The first section of this course provides an introduction to key frameworks and concepts relevant to public health ethics. The remaining part of the course considers ethical dilemmas across resource allocation and distributive justice, individual rights versus the common good, health promotion and disease prevention, free markets versus social justice, research ethics, emerging public health technologies and interventions, and public health and the environment.
PH 413.pre: must be enrolled in the MPH program (PB91, PB87, PB88, PB90, and PB75) or program approval.

PH 415.desc: This course will provide an in-depth overview of modern epidemiologic concepts, including fundamentals of causal inference; quantitative measures of occurrence, association, and effect; epidemiologic study design; epidemiologic data analysis; sources of bias in epidemiologic studies; and design and analytic strategies for the evaluation and mitigation of bias in epidemiologic studies.
PH 415.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401.

PH 417.desc: This is an MPH-level course designed to introduce topics in cardiovascular disease epidemiology using the following definition of epidemiology as a guide: Epidemiology is the study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations, and the application of this study to the control of health problems. As such, the course provides an overview of the prevalence, incidence, and key risk factors for major cardiovascular diseases.
PH 417.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401.

PH 417R.desc: This is an MPH-level course designed to introduce topics in cardiovascular disease epidemiology using the following definition of epidemiology as a guide: Epidemiology is the study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations, and the application of this study to the control of health problems. As such, the course provides an overview of the prevalence, incidence, and key risk factors for major cardiovascular diseases.
PH 417R.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Students may only receive credit for one of these courses: PH 417, PH 417R, or FMPH 417.
PH 417R.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Epidemiology)

PH 418.desc: Designed to increase understanding of the history, classification, surveillance, prevention, and control of major and emerging infectious diseases. Lectures, assignments, and discussions will also introduce students to methods of particular relevance to infectious disease epidemiology.
PH 418.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401.

PH 419.desc: Students will understand and conduct advanced bio-statistical analyses including: multiple linear and logistic regression, survival analysis, Cox and extended Cox regression, and longitudinal data analysis. Students will analyze data using these techniques and learn to program using a statistical software package (e.g., R). Issues such as confounding, missing data, and causal inference will be discussed.
PH 419.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 400 or PH 400.

PH 420.t: Introduction to Infectious Disease Epidemic and Economic Modeling for Health Policymaking
PH 420.desc: This course provides an introduction to infectious disease epidemic and cost-effectiveness modeling, with focus on applications to inform health policymaking. This didactic and computer lab-based course will cover basic models for human infectious disease transmission, model parameterization, calibration to surveillance data, projecting the epidemic impact of interventions, and cost-effectiveness modeling of health interventions. Students will learn how to code and analyze models in MATLAB.
PH 420.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB90, and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Students can’t receive credit for PH 420 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Introduction to Infectious Disease Epidemic and Economic Modeling for Health Policymaking.”

PH 425.desc: This course focuses on public health approaches to studying mental illnesses nationally and globally. Course content will include an overview of global mental health epidemiology; research methods; vulnerable populations, such as refugees and immigrants; and the challenges and future opportunities to address the mental illness epidemic, taking into consideration the social and cultural diversity within study populations.
PH 425.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB89, and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401.

PH 426.t: Public Mental and Behavior Health and Addiction
PH 426.desc: This course introduces key aspects of mental and behavioral health as well as the etiology, risk factors, and impact of mental disorders in public health. The focus will be given to the link between mental and physical health and the impact of mental health on health behavior and outcomes. Mental and behavioral health in relation to substance use and addiction will be covered. Intervention strategies to improve mental and behavioral health will be introduced.
PH 426.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB89) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 402 or PH 402.

PH 427.t: Mental Health Across the Life Course
PH 427.desc: This course examines mental health from infancy through childhood into adulthood and aging. Students will learn how perturbations in mental health manifest differently at different developmental stages over the life course. The course will also cover how early life exposures to stressful circumstances can lead to symptoms, disorder, or disease and how these manifest themselves across development. Students will explore potential strategies for identification of risk, prevention, and intervention.
PH 427.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB89) or program approval.
PH 427.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Public Mental Health)

PH 428.t: Dissemination and Implementation, Policy, and Health Services in Mental Health
PH 428.desc: This course will use a dissemination and implementation science methodology and lens to address the gap between promising research results for mental health and their successful translation into improved individual, community, and population health. Real-world case examples and a multidisciplinary approach will be used to discuss and address factors that impact the adoption, implementation, and sustained use of specific health-related interventions.
PH 428.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB88, and PB89) or program approval.

PH 429.desc: This course offers a window into the patterns, drivers, and consequences of substance use from a public health perspective. It also introduces various prevention, treatment, and harm reduction approaches. Through assessment of current epidemiologic data, application of conceptual frameworks, engagement with researchers and practitioners, and reflection on prevention, treatment, and harm reduction policies and strategies, we will explore the complexity of substance use and population health.
PH 429.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB89). Students cannot receive credit for PH 429 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Substance Use and Population Health.”
PH 429.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Behavior), MPH(Public Mental Health)

PH 430.desc: This course will introduce students to the field of precision health and will provide a broad overview of a variety of emerging technologies (artificial intelligence, informatics, big data and data science, genomics, spatial data, digital health, predictive analytics). Students will be prompted to consider the applications to public health policy and practice.
PH 430.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB90) or program approval.

PH 431.desc: The course introduces students to informatics concepts, techniques, and systems used in public health practice. The course covers systems and data standards used in vital statistics, immunization tracking, disease surveillance, disease outbreak management, electronic laboratory reporting, and disease registries. The course provides students experience with real world clinical data sets, relational and NoSQL database systems, and geographic information systems for public health data analysis.
PH 431.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB90) or program approval.

PH 440.desc: This course will introduce key concepts in health economics and apply these concepts to better understand and evaluate health policy issues in the U.S. health-care system. It will also introduce basic microeconomic analysis tools from the perspective of public health. Module 1 gives an overview of the U.S. health-care system and introduces microeconomic tools. Module 2 examines key players in the U.S. health-care system. Module 3 introduces economic evaluation tools and health policy issues.
PH 440.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88) and successfully completed FMPH 405 or PH 405.

PH 441.t: The Organization and Financing of the U.S. Health-Care System
PH 441.desc: Students will learn about the organization and financing of health services in the United States and the implications of system characteristics for quality, equity, and health-care costs; develop an understanding of how health policy decisions are made in the United States; and learn how health-care financing in the US compares with other countries around the world. Students will develop the background and skills to solve a range of problems in the fields of health policy and public health.
PH 441.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88) and successfully completed FMPH 405 or PH 405.
PH 441.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Policy)

PH 442.desc: This course introduces master’s students to qualitative research methods, emphasizing the strategies and applications of this methodology in public health, health justice, and community-engaged research. Through lectures, group work, interactive sessions, and practical exercises, students will gain foundational knowledge and skills in qualitative research. Topics also include theoretical foundations of research, biocultural ethics, and the advantages of numerous qualitative inquiry techniques.
PH 442.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB88). Students cannot receive credit for PH 442 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “Qualitative Research Methods.”
PH 442.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Policy)

PH 45.t: Introduction to Methods and Ethics in Public Health Research
PH 45.desc: This course will lay a foundation for understanding how to conduct research to answer questions about public health. It aims to teach students why research is done the way it is, what questions we can and can’t answer, and the methodological and ethical limits that must be considered along the way. Students will learn to think critically about the implications and limitations of existing research, and to form their own research questions about public health and the ways to investigate answers.

PH 460.desc: The focus of this project-based class is on teaching students fundamentals in design, with a particular focus on human-centered design and community-centered design. By the end of the course, students will have developed personal skills in using their chosen design approach (human- or community-centered design) and worked to advance and provide support to real-world partners of the professor. Students will also engage in a self-study project.
PH 460.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB90) or program approval.

PH 461.desc: Students will be introduced to and discuss important issues in public health in an interactive format with the MPH director, other FMPH faculty, and public health professionals from the San Diego public health community. Each week the class will focus on a different topic and the career path of one or more public health researchers or practitioners.
PH 461.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

PH 462.desc: This course will focus on the health and economic burden of non-communicable diseases (NCD) globally, understanding global patterns of major diseases and disease categories (cancer, CVD, diabetes, obesity) and health behaviors (smoking, diet, physical activity), global health policy and advocacy, and intervention strategies and evaluation of health programs related to global NCD. We will cover select global health issues in a format allowing for in-depth discussion.
PH 462.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

PH 463.t: VIIDAI: Public Health Field Practice in Baja
PH 463.desc: Students will develop an understanding of field epidemiology, surveillance, survey development, data collection, analysis, and presentation. They may also be exposed to planning, implementing, and evaluating age- and culturally-appropriate health promotion interventions. They will learn about cultural awareness, international travel safety, gain collaborative group experience with other institutions to carry out duties that will be put into practice during the class field trip.
PH 463.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91). Students cannot receive credit for PH 463 if they have already completed FMPH 491 subtitled “VIIDAI: Public Health Field Practice in Baja.”

PH 480.t: Introduction to Foundation and Government Grant Writing (Non-NIH)
PH 480.desc: Students learn the skill of grant writing as used by academics, practitioners, and leaders of the public health community to support program development and implementation, technical assistance and capacity building, resource development, research projects, training programs, and other areas. Students will learn strategies for successful teamwork and be introduced to strategies to identify and respond to grant opportunities using a data-driven and theoretically sound approach.
PH 480.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91).

PH 491.desc: Course will cover various topics in the field of public health. May be taken for credit up to twelve times for a maximum of forty-eight units.
PH 491.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.
PH 491.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Behavior), MPH(Health Policy), MPH(Public Mental Health), MPH(Tech&Precision Health), MPH(Epidemiology)

PH 496A.desc: This course is required prior to starting an MPH practicum. This course seeks to expose students to leadership principles and reinforce effective skills necessary at their field site and in their future careers by utilizing a blend of reflective individual and module-based activities to improve written and oral communication skills prior to their practicum. Students will also learn about the various fields and organizations in public health as they explore potential practicum opportunities.
PH 496A.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91).

PH 496B.desc: This course provides MPH students the opportunity to participate in a short-term, field-based public health or population-based experience. Students will engage in a field experience in collaboration with a sponsoring organization and qualified site mentor. Students are expected to apply theory, skills, and training acquired through the public health course work within a real-life setting. Students will develop written and oral communication skills that employ public health concepts and methods.
PH 496B.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91).
PH 496B.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Behavior), MPH(Health Policy), MPH(Public Mental Health), MPH(Tech&Precision Health), MPH(Epidemiology)

PH 498.desc: Independent study under the guidance of a Wertheim School of Public Health faculty member. May be taken for credit up to twelve times for a maximum of forty-eight units.

PH 499.desc: Students complete their capstone/thesis, and potentially submit their capstone/thesis for publication and/or present their capstone/thesis to stakeholders. May be taken for credit up to six times.
PH 499.pre: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.
PH 499.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Health Behavior), MPH(Health Policy), MPH(Public Mental Health), MPH(Tech&Precision Health), MPH(Epidemiology)

PH 50.desc: This course explores historical and current interactions, achievements, and challenges of primary care and public health. It will analyze the impact of common medical conditions such as obesity, diabetes, mental health disorders, and others on individuals, their families, and society. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 50. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 50 and PH 50.

PH 509.desc: This course is for graduate students wanting to develop skills and knowledge to become a teaching assistant or as preparation for an academic teaching career. The course covers the practice and theory of educating others, curriculum and instructional design, and teaching best practices.

PH 80.t: Racism as a Public Health Crisis
PH 80.desc: Recently, municipalities around the country have formally declared racism as a public health crisis. What does this mean? We will discuss race, racism, racial health disparities, and the nature of public health crises. Students will practice scientific writing in groups and individually.

PH 88.t: Learning Sustainable Well-Being: Compassion for Self and Others, a Public Health Perspective
PH 88.desc: This experiential course teaches the art of practicing psychological well-being, based on Eastern and Western approaches (e.g., mindfulness, positive psychology, cognitive therapy, neuroscience, theatre and art), from the perspective of public health. Each week there is a short lecture on a given topic, combined with workshop-style exercises. This course is part of the Learning Sustainable Well-being Program. Visit lsw.ucsd.edu for more information.

PH 90.desc: This seminar-style course offers students the opportunity to explore key areas of public health, covering foundational principles across a variety of topics. Subjects range and may include, but are not limited to, career pathways in public health, strategies for maintaining well-being and academic success, mental health awareness and support, sexual health and reproductive rights, mindfulness practices, financial wellness, stress management, and more.

PH 91.desc: Selected topics in the field of public health.
PH 91.res: Limited to class level: Freshman, Junior, Sophomore, Senior

PH 95.desc: This course is designed for first-year students and first-year transfer students who are interested in pursuing medicine and becoming physicians. Learn what it takes to prepare for medical school as well as what it takes to be a competitive applicant. We’ll cover everything from academic requirements, timeline, and MCAT to obtaining relevant experiences (i.e., healthcare, service, leadership, and research), letters of evaluation, the fifteen core competencies, and more.

PH 98.desc: Investigation of public health topics through directed reading and discussion by a small group of students under supervision of a faculty member. Opportunities can also include experiential and research components. May be taken for credit three times.
PH 98.pre: completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

PH 99.desc: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. May be taken for credit three times.
PH 99.pre: completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

PH 120R.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior

PH 198.res: Limited to class level: Junior, Senior

PH 223.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate, Medical, Pharmacy; Not open to academic level: Undergraduate

PH 433.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Master of Public Health, MPH(Tech&Precision Health)
